observations: The function has NO vendor census record, so no source hash can be bound the census way; the body hash is computed directly from the binary over the FDE range. The FDE is 2868 bytes (0x61c0180..0x61c0cb4); earlier packets quoted 3244 B, which does not match the FDE range and is corrected here.

The enclosing signature is pinned by the census symbol of the 0x61c1210 lambda: Comparator::CreateFromString(const ConfigOptions&, const std::string&, const Comparator**). The third parameter is a raw pointer-to-pointer, matching the v8.1.1 declaration (comparator.h:61-63, const Comparator**; no shared_ptr overload in v8.1.1).

Status is 16 bytes in this build (code @0, subcode @1, severity @2, retryable @3, data_loss @4, scope @5, state_ @8 as a unique_ptr<const char[]>), pinned by the Status ctor at 0x61cf670 and confirmed by upstream status.h. ok() is a single-byte test on the code. The sret return explains the epilogue 'mov %rbx,%rax; ret' (rbx holds the hidden return pointer) and the same pattern in the AsCustomRawPtr _M_invoke caller.

The bytewise name compare reuses the overlapping-fragment trick from #5958's block 1: the 16-byte stores at +0 ('leveldb.') and +8 ('Bytewise') are followed by 8-byte XORs at +10 ('tewiseCo') and +18 ('mparator'), so the 'tewise' run is checked twice with identical bytes. The reverse name uses non-overlapping chunks plus the single 'r' byte check at +32.

The error Status construction reuses the zeroed id length as the subcode: the path is only reached when the id length is 0 (the 0x61c0396 jne skips it otherwise), so edx (the length) is 0 = SubCode kNone at the Status ctor call. The msg2 slice is the id string with length 0, so the rendered message is exactly the 20-byte literal 'Cannot reset object '.

NewStaticObject is a member function on config_options.registry: the binary loads the shared_ptr data pointer at config_options+0x40 as `this`, and passes the parsed name (rsp+0xf0) as the single target string; the factory is invoked as factory(target, guard, &errmsg). (Correction: earlier packets described a separate 'registry id' string at +0x40; upstream convenience.h pins +0x40 as the registry shared_ptr.)

The swallow after NewStaticObject reads the byte at config_options+1 (ignore_unsupported_options, upstream default true) and requires code 3 (kNotSupported). ConfigureNewObject's Status is NOT subject to the swallow: a configure failure is returned as-is.

The GetOptionsMap call passes the current *result as the 'customizable' argument. On entry *result is expected to be null (the caller passes a fresh slot), so in practice this is a null customizable; the binary does not null-check it first.

The caller (0x607df90 _M_invoke) is the only reference to this function in the whole .text: exactly 1 E8 call, 0 tail jumps, 0 LEA refs (Capstone-validated census). The 'id' special case lives in the caller, not in CreateFromString.

The U64Ts branch's zero-length edge: when the id length equals the cached-name length (both 0) the code jumps straight to the factory (0x61c0587 je 0x61c0aa0) without calling memcmp -- a memcmp of length 0 is equal by definition. The cached name is 32 chars in practice, so this edge is unreachable with the real cache.
